key_terms.meaning: Four diodes give full-wave DC; ideal V<sub>dc</sub> = 2V<sub>m</sub>/π for a single-phase bridge.
Reverse voltage a diode must block; bridge diode sees V<sub>m</sub>, centre-tap full-wave sees 2V<sub>m</sub>.
Output ripple frequency is f for half-wave and 2f for single-phase full-wave.
Shunt C holds output near V<sub>m</sub>; diode current becomes short and tall.
Series L blocks ripple and C bypasses remaining ripple; needs critical inductance.
Electrical delay from forward-voltage crossing to gate pulse; sets V<sub>dc</sub>.
All switches are thyristors; with active load V<sub>dc</sub> can go negative.
Thyristors and diodes mix; output has one voltage polarity and inherent freewheeling.
Load current stays above zero; ideal V<sub>dc</sub> depends on α, not load.
Number of DC pulses per supply cycle; ripple frequency = p f.
Six-pulse converter; ideal V<sub>dc</sub> = (3√3 V<sub>m</sub>/π) cos α for continuous current.
cos φ<sub>1</sub>, the cosine of angle between fundamental input current and voltage.
THD = √(Σ I<sub>n</sub>²)/I<sub>1</sub> for n ≥ 2; measures current distortion.
PF = P/S = (I<sub>1rms</sub>/I<sub>rms</sub>) cos φ<sub>1</sub> for sinusoidal voltage.
Supply inductance that slows current transfer and causes overlap.
Angle when outgoing and incoming thyristors conduct together.
Average output loss proportional to L<sub>s</sub>, I<sub>d</sub> and supply frequency.
Two anti-parallel controlled bridges for four-quadrant operation.
Current between simultaneously enabled bridges; limited by a reactor.
Boost stage after diode bridge shapes input current sinusoidal and regulates DC bus.

takeaways: A diode rectifier has a fixed average voltage set by supply peak and topology; no gate control can change it.
A capacitor filter raises no-load voltage and narrows diode current pulses; an LC filter smooths current but needs proper inductor design.
Phase control by α moves the average output continuously and can make it negative when the load can supply energy.
A p-pulse converter has output ripple at p times supply frequency; six-pulse three-phase is the common industrial case.
Power factor is not just cos α: input current harmonics also reduce PF.
Source inductance creates overlap, lowers average output with load, and limits the maximum inverter angle.
A dual converter gives reversible voltage and current; circulating-current mode is fast but needs a reactor.
A PFC rectifier makes input current follow the sine voltage, giving near-unity power factor and low THD.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask for an average-voltage derivation for a given topology and load, sketched waveforms, and then a discussion of displacement factor, ripple, harmonics and source-inductance drop.

outline: Ripple factor from rms and average

outline: Commutation drop grows with I<sub>d</sub> and L<sub>s</sub>

Positive, zero and negative average cases

glossary.def: Circuit that converts AC to DC.
Mean of output voltage over one period.
Rms value divided by average value.
Rms of AC ripple divided by average DC.
Maximum reverse voltage across an off diode or thyristor.
Diode that carries inductive load current when the main switch turns off.
Shunt capacitor that stores charge and reduces output ripple.
Series inductor plus shunt capacitor that blocks ripple.
Minimum choke inductance that keeps an LC filter in continuous current at a given load.
Four-layer controlled switch that latches on with a gate pulse and turns off when current falls.
Delaying thyristor turn-on within each supply half-cycle to control average voltage.
Delay angle α measured from the natural commutation point.
Converter with both diodes and thyristors; output voltage has one polarity.
Converter with all thyristors; can invert with an active load.
Load current remains above zero throughout the cycle.
Load current reaches zero before the next firing, so output voltage depends on load.
Number of output pulses per supply cycle.
Transfer of load current from one device to the next.
Angle during which two devices conduct together because of source inductance.
Cosine of the phase angle between fundamental input current and supply voltage.
Ratio of harmonic rms current to fundamental rms current.
Real power divided by apparent power.
Two anti-parallel controlled rectifiers that allow reversible voltage and current.
Current that flows between the two bridges of a dual converter when both are enabled.
Input shaping that makes line current sinusoidal and in phase with voltage.
Diode bridge plus boost converter that regulates DC output and shapes input current.
